devotions.title: Be still
devotions.body: Psalm 46 was written for people whose world was shaking. Nations were in uproar and the ground itself seemed unsafe. Into that turmoil God speaks: stop striving, and know that He is God, exalted among the nations and over all the earth. The verse is first a declaration of His sovereignty. In a world shaken by conflict and uncertainty, He alone rules, and we can stop striving to control what belongs to Him and rest in His authority. Here is one way to apply it. Many of us begin the day already running, with a phone in our hand before a prayer is on our lips. Today, before you answer one message, sit quietly for two minutes and tell God, “You are God, and I am not.” The problems may be the same when you stand up. You will not be.
devotions.prayer: Father, quiet my heart today. Teach me to stop striving and to trust that You are God over everything I am facing. In Jesus’ name, amen.
devotions.question: What is one thing you need to stop striving over and place in God’s hands today?

devotions.title: Trust with all your heart
devotions.body: Solomon does not tell us to throw away our understanding. He tells us not to lean our whole weight on it. Our understanding is limited: we see today, and God sees the end from the beginning. Trusting with all the heart means we bring Him into every part of life, not only the religious parts. Work, money, marriage, children and plans are all “ways” in which we can acknowledge Him. The promise is that He makes the path straight. That does not always mean easy. It means He leads us where we need to go. Before your next decision today, large or small, pause and ask, “Lord, what would honour You here?”
devotions.prayer: Lord, I confess that I often lean on my own thinking. Today I choose to trust You in every area of my life. Direct my steps. Amen.
devotions.question: Which area of your life is hardest to trust God with right now?

devotions.title: First things first
devotions.body: Jesus spoke these words to ordinary people who worried about food and clothing. He did not say those needs were unimportant. He said the Father already knows about them. Worry puts tomorrow’s trouble on today’s shoulders, and we were never built to carry both. The answer Jesus gives is an order of priority: seek God’s kingdom and His righteousness first, and trust the Father with the rest. Ask yourself what gets the first and best part of your day. If it is the news, the bank balance or the inbox, your heart will follow it. Give God the first part of today, and deal with today only.
devotions.prayer: Father, You know what I need before I ask. Help me to seek Your kingdom first and to leave tomorrow with You. Amen.
devotions.question: What would “seeking first the kingdom” look like in your day today?

devotions.title: Prayer instead of worry
devotions.body: Paul wrote this from prison, so it is not advice from a comfortable man. He gives a simple exchange: bring every anxious thought to God as a request, and bring it with thanksgiving. Thanksgiving matters because it reminds us of what God has already done while we wait for what He will do. The promise is not that every situation changes at once. The promise is that God’s peace will stand guard over our hearts and minds in Christ Jesus, like a soldier at a gate. Today, each time a worry rises, turn it into one sentence of prayer and one sentence of thanks.
devotions.prayer: Lord, I bring You the things that trouble me today. Thank You for Your faithfulness in the past. Guard my heart and mind with Your peace. Amen.
devotions.question: What is one thing you can thank God for today, even while you are waiting?

devotions.title: Do not fear
devotions.body: God spoke these words to Israel when they felt small among powerful nations. Notice that the reason not to fear is not that the danger is unreal. The reason is a Person: “I am with you… I am your God.” Then come three promises: He will strengthen, He will help, and He will uphold. Fear tells us we are alone and that everything depends on us. God answers both lies. Whatever you face today, a diagnosis, a debt, a difficult conversation, you do not walk into it alone. Read this verse aloud and remember the God who remained faithful to His people. If you belong to Christ, you can face today trusting His presence and faithfulness.
devotions.prayer: God, thank You that You are with me. Where I am weak, strengthen me. Where I am afraid, hold me up with Your hand. Amen.
devotions.question: Where do you most need God’s strength this week?

devotions.title: New every morning
devotions.body: These words stand in the middle of one of the saddest books in the Bible. Jerusalem was in ruins, and the writer was grieving. Yet he chose to call something to mind: the steadfast love of the Lord never ceases. Hope did not come from his circumstances. It came from what he remembered about God. Yesterday’s failure does not use up today’s mercy. You did not wake up this morning on leftover grace. If you are carrying guilt or disappointment from yesterday, bring it to the Lord now and receive today’s mercy for today.
devotions.prayer: Faithful Father, thank You that Your mercies are new this morning. I receive them. Help me to begin again with You today. Amen.
devotions.question: How have you seen God’s faithfulness in a hard season?

devotions.title: Stay connected
devotions.body: Jesus spoke this on the night before the cross, as He prepared His disciples for life without His physical presence. A branch does not produce fruit by trying harder. It bears fruit by staying joined to the vine. Our first calling is not to work for Jesus but to remain in Him: in His word, in prayer, in obedience and in fellowship with His people. Fruit then grows as a result. Apart from Him, Jesus says, we can do nothing of lasting spiritual value. If you feel dry or tired in your faith, do not start with more activity. Start by returning to Him.
devotions.prayer: Lord Jesus, You are the vine and I am a branch. Keep me close to You today, and let my life bear fruit that pleases the Father. Amen.
devotions.question: What helps you stay close to Jesus through a busy week?

devotions.title: Ask for wisdom
devotions.body: James wrote to believers facing trials, and he knew they would need more than information. They would need wisdom, which is the skill of living God’s way in real situations. The good news is how God gives it: generously and without reproach. He does not scold us for asking again. Many of us ask friends, search the internet and lie awake thinking before we ever ask God. Reverse the order today. Name the decision in front of you, ask God plainly for wisdom, then open the Scriptures and seek godly counsel, expecting Him to guide you.
devotions.prayer: Father, I need Your wisdom. Thank You that You give generously. Show me the right way in the decision I am facing. Amen.
devotions.question: Is there a decision you would like the community to pray about with you?

devotions.title: Light for the next step
devotions.body: In the ancient world a lamp lit only the few steps ahead of the traveller. God’s word works the same way. It rarely shows us the whole road for the next ten years, but it gives enough light for the next faithful step. We often want the full map before we obey. God gives a lamp and asks us to walk. The lamp only helps if we carry it. A Bible that stays closed gives no light. Read one passage today slowly, and ask, “What does this show me about God, and what step should I take?”
devotions.prayer: Lord, thank You for Your word. Give me a hunger to read it and the courage to walk in the light You give. Amen.
devotions.question: Which verse has guided you recently?

devotions.title: Come and rest
devotions.body: Jesus gives this invitation to people worn out by burdens, including the heavy religious rules others had laid on them. He does not say, “Try harder.” He says, “Come to me.” Rest is found in a Person. Notice that He still speaks of a yoke. Jesus does not invite us into a life without obedience. He invites us to become His disciples, to learn from His gentle and lowly heart, and to find rest under His gracious leadership. If your soul is tired today, more sleep may help the body, but only Jesus gives rest to the soul. Come to Him as you are.
devotions.prayer: Lord Jesus, I come to You tired. I lay down the burdens I was never meant to carry. Teach me Your ways and give rest to my soul. Amen.
devotions.question: What burden do you need to bring to Jesus today?

devotions.title: God is at work
devotions.body: This verse does not say that all things are good. Sickness, loss and betrayal are not good in themselves, and Paul knew suffering well. The promise is that God works in all things for the good of those who love Him. The next verse tells us what that good is: being shaped into the likeness of His Son. So the promise is larger than comfort or success. God is able to take even what was meant for harm and use it to make us more like Jesus. You may not see how today. Faith holds on to who God is while the story is still being written.
devotions.prayer: Father, I do not understand everything I am going through. I trust that You are at work in it. Make me more like Jesus through it. Amen.
devotions.question: Can you look back and see how God used a hard time for good?

devotions.title: He cares for you
devotions.body: Peter wrote to believers who were suffering for their faith. Just before this verse he calls them to humble themselves under God’s mighty hand. Casting our cares on God is part of that humility. Pride says, “I can carry this myself.” Humility says, “Lord, this is too heavy for me.” The reason we can hand our worries over is simple and personal: He cares for you. Not for people in general, for you. Name your cares one at a time in prayer today, and picture yourself placing each one in His hands. When you find you have picked one up again, give it back.
devotions.prayer: Lord, I give You the worries I have been carrying. Thank You that You care for me. Help me to leave them with You. Amen.
devotions.question: What care would you like to hand over to God today?

devotions.title: Strong and courageous
devotions.body: Joshua had a great task in front of him. Moses was dead, and the people now looked to him to lead them into the land. God did not tell Joshua he was talented enough. He gave a command and a reason: be strong and courageous, because the Lord your God is with you wherever you go. Courage in Scripture is not the absence of fear. It is obedience in the presence of fear, resting on the presence of God. In the verses before, God ties this courage to keeping His word close. What step of obedience have you been putting off because you feel afraid?
devotions.prayer: Lord, give me courage to obey You today. Thank You that You go with me wherever I go. Amen.
devotions.question: What step of obedience needs courage from you this week?

devotions.title: Saved by grace
devotions.body: This is the heart of the gospel. We are saved by grace, through faith, and even this is God’s gift, so that nobody can boast. We did not earn our place with God by good behaviour, church attendance or religious effort. Jesus earned it for us by His death and resurrection, and we receive it by trusting Him. This sets us free in two ways. We are free from pride, because we contributed nothing. We are free from despair, because our standing does not rest on our performance. Verse 10 adds that good works follow as the fruit of salvation, never its cause. Rest today in what Christ has done.
devotions.prayer: Father, thank You for the gift of salvation. I did not earn it and I cannot repay it. Let my life be a thank-offering to You. Amen.
devotions.question: How did you first come to understand God’s grace?

devotions.title: The Lord is my shepherd
devotions.body: David knew shepherding from the inside. He had fed, led and defended sheep himself. When he calls the Lord his shepherd, he is saying that God personally provides, guides and protects. Notice the change in verse 4. In the green pastures David speaks about God: “He leads me.” In the dark valley he speaks to God: “You are with me.” Hard seasons often bring us closer than easy ones. The psalm does not promise that we will avoid life’s darkest valleys. It assures us that the Lord remains our Shepherd even there. His presence is our comfort when the road is difficult and the outcome uncertain.
devotions.prayer: Lord, You are my shepherd. Lead me today, restore my soul, and stay close to me in every valley. Amen.
devotions.question: Which line of Psalm 23 speaks to you most today, and why?

devotions.title: Do not give up
devotions.body: Paul uses the picture of a farmer. Nobody plants seed in the morning and looks for a harvest by evening. There is a long season between sowing and reaping, and most of the work in that season is unseen. Doing good can feel like that: praying for a family member for years, serving faithfully with no thanks, choosing honesty when it costs you. Paul admits that we can grow weary. His encouragement is that the harvest belongs to God’s timing. It may not look like the result we pictured, and our calling is to remain faithful even when we cannot yet see the results. Your labour in the Lord is not wasted. Keep sowing today.
devotions.prayer: Father, strengthen me where I am tired of doing good. Help me to keep sowing and to trust You with the harvest. Amen.
devotions.question: Where do you need encouragement to keep going?

devotions.title: Forgiven and cleansed
devotions.body: John wrote this to believers. Christians still sin, and pretending otherwise only deceives ourselves. The answer is not hiding, and it is not punishing ourselves. The answer is confession: agreeing with God about what we have done. The promise rests on His character. He is faithful, so He will keep His word. He is just, because Jesus has already paid for that sin on the cross. He both forgives and cleanses. If something has been weighing on your conscience, do not carry it one more day. Bring it into the light before God now.
devotions.prayer: Lord, I confess my sin to You and hide nothing. Thank You that You are faithful and just to forgive me and make me clean. Amen.
devotions.question: What has helped you to receive God’s forgiveness and not keep carrying guilt?

devotions.title: Forgive as you were forgiven
devotions.body: Paul is describing life inside the church, among people who will sometimes disappoint each other. He does not pretend the complaint is imaginary. He says that where there is a complaint, we are to bear with one another and forgive. The measure is the hard part: as the Lord has forgiven you. Forgiveness means refusing to nurture revenge and entrusting justice to God. It does not erase the seriousness of the wrong, remove appropriate consequences, or automatically restore trust. We forgive from a full account, because we have been forgiven far more.
devotions.prayer: Lord, You have forgiven me so much. Give me grace to forgive the person who hurt me, and heal what is wounded in me. Amen.
devotions.question: What has God taught you about forgiving others?

devotions.title: Come boldly
devotions.body: The verses before this one tell us why we can come. Jesus is our great high priest, who was tempted in every way as we are, yet without sin. He understands weakness from the inside. So the throne we approach is a throne of grace, not of rejection. We are invited to come with confidence, not because we have been good this week, but because of Him. Two things wait for us there: mercy for where we have failed, and grace to help in our time of need. Do not wait until you feel worthy to pray. Come now.
devotions.prayer: Lord Jesus, thank You for opening the way to the Father. I come with confidence for mercy and for help today. Amen.
devotions.question: What do you need to bring to the throne of grace today?

devotions.title: Strength in weakness
devotions.body: Paul asked the Lord three times to remove his “thorn in the flesh.” God’s answer was not removal but a promise: His grace is sufficient, and His power is made perfect in weakness. That is a hard answer and a good one. We usually think God can use us most when we are strong. Often it is the reverse. Weakness keeps us depending on Him, and His strength is seen most clearly where ours ends. If you have prayed for something to change and it has not yet, this does not mean God has left you. His grace is enough for today.
devotions.prayer: Lord, where I am weak, be strong in me. Let Your grace be enough for me today, and let Christ be seen in my life. Amen.
devotions.question: Where have you seen God’s strength in a time of weakness?

devotions.title: A renewed mind
devotions.body: After eleven chapters on God’s mercy, Paul turns to how we should live in response. The world around us is always pressing us into its shape, through what we watch, read and hear repeated. Paul says do not be conformed, but be transformed, and he names where the change happens: the renewing of the mind. Lasting change in behaviour begins with a change in thinking. As God’s word reshapes how we think, we become able to recognise His will, which is good, acceptable and perfect. Ask yourself today what has been shaping your thinking most this week, and whether it draws you toward Christ.
devotions.prayer: Father, renew my mind by Your word and Your Spirit. Change the way I think, so that I may know and do Your will. Amen.
devotions.question: What helps you to fill your mind with God’s truth during the week?

devotions.title: Made by God
devotions.body: David looks back to before his birth and sees God’s hands at work, forming him with care. His response is praise. Your life is not an accident, and your worth was settled by your Maker long before you achieved anything. Many of us measure ourselves by appearance, income or the opinions of others, and we come up short. This psalm gives a different measure. The God who made the stars also made you, knows you completely, and has not looked away. Thank Him today for the life He gave you, and treat others as people He made with the same care.
devotions.prayer: Creator God, thank You for making me and knowing me. Help me to see myself and others the way You do. Amen.
devotions.question: What does it mean to you that God knows you completely?

devotions.title: What the Lord requires
devotions.body: In Micah’s day people asked what offering would be large enough to please God. Thousands of rams? Rivers of oil? God’s answer was not a bigger sacrifice but a way of life: do justice, love kindness, and walk humbly with your God. These three belong together. Justice is treating people rightly and fairly. Kindness is faithful, merciful love. Humility is walking with God day by day, aware of our need of Him. We do not do these things to earn salvation. They are the life that flows from knowing the God who has shown us mercy. Choose one of the three to practise on purpose today.
devotions.prayer: Lord, teach me to act justly, to love mercy and to walk humbly with You in the ordinary moments of today. Amen.
devotions.question: Which of the three, justice, kindness or humility, is God working on in you?

devotions.title: Let your light shine
devotions.body: Jesus does not tell His followers to try to become light. He says they are the light of the world. A lamp is lit to be seen, not hidden under a basket. Notice the purpose He gives. Our good works are seen so that people give glory to our Father in heaven, not to us. Your light may be patience with a difficult colleague, honesty when no one is checking, or kindness to a neighbour. Someone near you may never open a Bible, but they are reading your life. Ask God to show you one person to serve today.
devotions.prayer: Father, let my life point people to You. Show me one person I can serve today for Your glory. Amen.
devotions.question: Who showed you the light of Christ before you believed?

devotions.title: Words that build up
devotions.body: Paul gives a test for every sentence before it leaves our mouths, or our keyboards. Does it build up? Does it fit the need of the moment? Does it give grace to those who hear? Words can heal a person or wound them for years. The verse covers more than swearing. Gossip, harsh criticism and careless joking can all tear down. The next verse warns us not to grieve the Holy Spirit, which shows how seriously God takes our speech. Today, before you speak or post, pause and ask whether your words will give grace. Then look for one person to encourage on purpose.
devotions.prayer: Lord, set a guard over my mouth. Let my words today build others up and give grace to those who hear. Amen.
devotions.question: Is there someone you can encourage today? Tell us what encouragement has meant to you.

devotions.title: Rejoice, pray, give thanks
devotions.body: Three short commands, and each has a word that stretches us: always, without ceasing, in all circumstances. Paul is not asking us to pretend that hard things are pleasant. He says to give thanks in all circumstances, not for all of them. We can thank God in the middle of difficulty because He is still good, still present and still working. Praying without ceasing does not mean never stopping to do anything else. It means living in an ongoing conversation with God through the day. Paul says plainly that this is God’s will for us in Christ Jesus. Start now with three things you are thankful for.
devotions.prayer: Father, I thank You for Your goodness to me. Teach me to rejoice, to keep praying and to give thanks whatever today brings. Amen.
devotions.question: Name three things you are thankful for today.

devotions.title: We need each other
devotions.body: The first readers of Hebrews were under pressure, and some had stopped meeting together. The writer tells them not to give up gathering, and gives the reason: we need to stir one another up to love and good works, and to encourage each other. Faith is personal, but it was never meant to be private. Alone, our love cools and our courage fades. Together, we are strengthened. This is why a community like ours exists, alongside your local church and never in place of it. When you pray for someone here, or share what God is teaching you, you are obeying this verse. Encourage one person today.
devotions.prayer: Lord, thank You for the family of believers. Show me who needs encouragement today, and use me to strengthen them. Amen.
devotions.question: Go to the Prayer Wall, pray for one request, and tap “I prayed.” Then tell us how we can pray for you.

devotions.title: He will finish what He started
devotions.body: Paul was confident about the Philippian believers, and his confidence was not in them. It was in God. The One who began a good work in them would bring it to completion at the day of Jesus Christ. The same is true for you. Your salvation was God’s work from the start, and He does not abandon what He begins. On days when you feel you are making little progress, remember that you are unfinished, not forsaken. God is patient and thorough. Co-operate with Him today in the one area where you know He is working.
devotions.prayer: Father, thank You that You finish what You begin. Keep working in me, and help me to yield to You today. Amen.
devotions.question: What is one area where you can see God has changed you?

devotions.title: Strength for the weary
devotions.body: Isaiah has just said that even young men grow tired and fall. Human strength runs out for everyone. Those who wait for the Lord receive something different: strength that is renewed. Waiting in Scripture is not passive. It is hopeful trust, looking to God and depending on Him. Notice the order in the verse: soaring, running, walking. Some days faith feels like flying. Most days it is the steady walk of not giving up. God gives strength for all three. If you are weary today, do not push harder in your own power. Wait on Him.
devotions.prayer: Lord, I am weary, and I wait for You. Renew my strength today, so that I can walk and not faint. Amen.
devotions.question: What does “waiting on the Lord” look like for you in this season?

devotions.title: The Lord bless you
devotions.body: God Himself gave these words to Aaron and his sons to speak over the people of Israel. It reveals His gracious character and His desire to dwell among His covenant people. The picture of His face shining on them is the picture of His favour and His nearness. As Christians, we receive God’s grace and peace through Jesus Christ, our great High Priest. As we close these thirty days, receive these words as God’s desire for you. Then do what the priests did, and speak blessing over someone else: your spouse, a child, a friend, or a member of this community.
devotions.prayer: Lord, bless and keep every member of this community. Make Your face shine on us, be gracious to us, and give us Your peace. Amen.
devotions.question: What has God taught you over these thirty days?
